rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). For PRS-comparable performance, only PGS001784 reports a covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only R2 (0.014661), but it comes from a pan-trait/global-biobank framework paper, which the provided domain_knowledge flags as systematically underperforming disease-focused models unless it has clearly superior endpoint/metric evidence. PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program/Mayo-VDB), reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and avoids reliance on full-model AUROC; this combination is the most coherent direct-disease evidence package in the context. Confidence is not high because several newer disease-focused candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) report only full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) without PRS-only metrics, and the relative standalone PRS contribution cannot be compared cleanly across models from the visible metadata. | Pairwise rerank promoted runner-up PGS001784 over primary PGS000753.

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches for the target alcohol dependence: PGS002738 and PGS002739 are explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"; PGS000201/PGS000202 are labeled "Problematic alcohol use" but their phenotyping_reported is also AUD (DSM-5 criteria count), making them concept-aligned. Among these, PGS002738 is best supported by the visible performance evidence because it reports a relatively strong case-control style discrimination signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900) and is developed from disease-relevant cohorts (MVP, UKB). However, the overall evidence remains limited for a high-confidence pick because none of the candidates report PRS-comparable AUC or PRS-only R2, covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 (reducing comparability), and the two 2020 PRS-CS scores provide only small incremental ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456) without clearer PRS-only metrics, leaving some unresolved uncertainty in cross-model comparability.
